rows.say: hey whats a good pasta for tonight
replies: Sam: Hey! Go with a simple garlic and olive oil spaghetti, or aglio e olio if you want the fancy name. It takes about 15 minutes and uses stuff you probably have already. Cook the garlic gently in the oil so it goes golden, not brown, because burnt garlic turns bitter. Add chili flakes and a splash of pasta water. From memory Check this
Alex: Salt the water until it tastes like mild sea water, and scoop out a mug before you drain. Toss the spaghetti in the pan with a splash of that water and the oil turns silky instead of greasy.
Robin: Just check who's at the table for allergies, and go easy on the chili flakes if kids are eating. Also, make the garlic oil fresh and cook it right away. Don't keep leftover garlic oil.

rows.say: and what wine goes with it
replies: Sam: A dry white is the easy win: Pinot Grigio, Vermentino, or a crisp Sauvignon Blanc. They're light and zippy, so they cut through the garlic and olive oil without bossing the dish around. Serve it well chilled. If you're a red person, go for something light like a Chianti, but skip anything big and oaky.
Robin: Just check, if anyone's pregnant, driving or on medication, skip the wine or keep it small. And if the dish has shellfish, a few wines can clash, so go easy there.
Alex: Chill the white about 2 hours in the fridge. In a rush, ice water with a big handful of salt does it in 20 minutes. Pull the red out for a bit too, slightly cool is perfect.

rows.say: Good afternoon. I would like to organise a small dinner for twelve colleagues near the theatre district in Manchester next month; could you please advise on how to choose a venue?
replies: Sam: Good afternoon. For twelve people near the theatre district, I would choose in this order. First, settle the date and a rough budget per head, then book early, since next month is the festive season and Manchester fills quickly. Then check these points: - Ask for a private room or a reserved section, so you can hear one another. - Confirm they take groups of twelve, and whether they require a set menu or a deposit. - Send the menu in advance and ask about dietary needs. - Look at the location: a walk of ten minutes or less from the theatre district suits colleagues arriving from work. - Check step-free access. After that, shortlist three venues and phone each one to compare. Next, I can ask Alex to draw up that shortlist. Next, Alex can draw up the shortlist of three venues. rows.say: My dad passed away last week and I have to say a few words at the funeral. I don't know where to start.
replies: Sam: I'm so sorry about your dad. Here's a simple way in. First, don't try to write the speech yet. Just jot down a few things, in any order: a story about him that people would recognize, something he always said or did, and what you'll miss most. Messy notes are fine. Then pick one story and let it carry the speech. Open with who you are to him, tell the story, and end with one line about what he gave you or what you'll hold onto. A few minutes is plenty. Reading it from paper is completely fine. What's one memory of him that came to mind first?
Pat: Whenever you're ready, send me your notes, however messy. I'll shape them into a plain speech of about three minutes, and it helps to read it aloud once to hear how it sounds.

chime.raw: [{"seat":"master","point":"Offer to shape their notes into a short, plain speech. Suggest reading it aloud once, and keeping it to about 3 minutes."}]

rows.say: quick - how long do I boil an egg for a soft yolk? running late
replies: Sam: About 6 to 6.5 minutes. Get the water boiling first, then lower the egg in gently, straight from the fridge. Pop it in cold water right after so it stops cooking. Peel it under the tap. rows.say: Is it safe to leave my dog in the car for ten minutes while I pop into a shop on a warm day?
replies: Sam: No, it isn't safe. Even ten minutes is risky on a warm day. A car heats up fast. On a day that feels mild outside, the inside can pass 40°C in about ten minutes. Cracking a window barely helps. Dogs cool down by panting, and in a hot car that stops working. Heatstroke can set in quickly and can kill, or cause lasting harm. Short-nosed breeds, puppies, older dogs and thick-coated dogs are at the most risk. First, if you can, take the dog in with you or choose a dog-friendly shop. Then, if neither works, run the errand another time, or go with someone who can wait outside with the dog. Next, if you ever see a dog in distress in a car, call the local emergency or animal-welfare number. ! Careful: Heatstroke can set in quickly and can kill or cause lasting harm. rows.say: Robin, is ten minutes really enough to hurt a dog?
replies: Robin: Just check this against what the vets say: yes, ten minutes can be enough to hurt a dog, and sometimes much less. On a warm day the inside of a car can climb 10°C or more in the first ten minutes, and most of that rise comes early. A dog can't sweat, so it relies on panting, and hot air makes that useless. Dogs with short noses, puppies, older dogs and heavy coats are hit hardest. It won't hurt every dog every time, but you can't tell beforehand which time it will. Heatstroke can do lasting damage.
